full_judgment:
2. Relevant facts necessary for disposal of this petition for leave to appeal are that the petitioner is engaged with liquor business and has been permitted for the possession and consumption of liquor in accordance with the provisions of section 11(1) of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990 and petitioner obtained the permit under the provision of East Bengal Excise (Foreign) and Country Liquor Prohibition and Restriction Rules, 1950 for the possession and consumption of liquor vide permit No.1/10-11 dated 01.07.2010. 

 8. Mr. A.F.M. Mesbahuddin, the learned senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that possession and consumption of liqueur are absolutely controlled and guided by the provisions of Narcotics Control Act, 1990, Narcotics Control Rules 1999 and the East Bengal Excise (Foreign and Country Liquor Prohibitions and Restriction) Rules 1950 but neither in the Narcotics Control Act, 1990, nor Narcotics Rules. 1999 nor the East Bengal Excise (Foreign and Country Liquor Prohibitions and Restrictions) Rules contain any provision for attachment of the photo of the permit holder with the permit and as such arrived at an erroneous decision. 

 9. He submitted further that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that permit for consumption and possession of liquor is granted under the provision of section 11 of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990 read with Rule 8 of the Narcotics Control Rules, 1999 and the East Bengal Excise (Foreign and Country Liquor Prohibitions and Restriction) Rules, 1950 but there is no provision for attachment of the photo of the permit holder with the permit in the Act and Rules and in view of such provisions the impugned order is liable to be set-aside. 

 10. The learned Advocate further submitted that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that the attachment of the photo of the permit holder with permit by Executive Order without amendment of the provisions of Narcotics Control Act, 1990 Narcotics Control Rules, 1999 and the East Bengal Excise (Foreign and Country Liquor Prohibitions and Restriction ) Rules, 1950 is absolutely without jurisdiction and without lawful authority and as such arrived at an erroneous decision.
